description_full: NerdWallet, Inc. operates a digital platform that provides financial guidance to consumers and small and mid-sized businesses (SMB) in the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Canada. It offers editorial and content publishing, a consumer and SMB financial education, tools, calculators, guides, and research published under the NerdWallet brand; Marketplace And Referral Services, a tool that enable users to compare, pre-qualify for, or connect with third-party providers of credit cards, consumer loans, small business loans, insurance, mortgages, financial services, and related products, as well as services including fundera, nerdwallet insurance services, nerdwallet advisory, and nerdwallet compare; and Financial Services, a brokerage and advisory services provided by insurance agency, loan and mortgage brokerages, and investment advisory subsidiaries. Additionally, the company provides finance and refinance facilities to students for education. NerdWallet, Inc. was founded in 2009 and is based in San Mateo, California.

financial_summary: NerdWallet, Inc. is a small-cap communication services business with a $504M market cap on $837M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +16% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +4.5pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 1% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $130M in free cash flow — roughly 16 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.70× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -18.0% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 13.9% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 5.8% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
